title: Commit a change and ignore the junk
setup: git init -q . && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
printf 'version 1\n' > app.txt && git add app.txt && git commit -qm 'Start app'
printf 'debug output\n' > debug.log && mkdir build && printf 'binary' > build/output.bin

checks.name: app.txt was changed in a new commit
checks.cmd: ! git diff --quiet $(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD) HEAD -- app.txt

checks.name: debug.log and build/ are not committed
debug.log and build/output.bin still exist on disk
nothing is left uncommitted (git status is clean)

hints: Run git status first: it lists the untracked files you need to deal with.
Two lines in .gitignore are enough: *.log and build/
Remember to add and commit .gitignore itself.
